Summerville strata are overlain by 4 m of thick-bedded
white channel sandstones with heavy mineral layers, the
lower MorrisonFormation,andinturnoverlain by82mof
variegated mudstones of the upper Morrison Formation. A
total of 68 samples were obtained in the Summerville
Formation, sampled from the contact with the Entrada
Formation uptothebasalMorrisonsandstones.Thesebeds
are nearly horizontal, dipping 5  to the northeast.

[9] A suite of 25 samples distributed stratigraphically
through both Summerville sections was thermally demag-
netized in 18 temperature increments between 150 C to
675 C.Fromtheresultingdata,therestofthesampleswere
thermally demagnetized in 10–12 increments each, begin-
ning at 300 C and extending through 670 C. About two
thirdsofthesamplesatbothsitesexhibitadirectionnearthe
axial dipole field direction as the first vector removed; that
magnetization is removed by 150 –200 C. Above 300 –
400 C, a number of samples display linear trends to the
origin, defining the characteristic directions for those sam-
ples; many of the samples display their characteristic
directions up to temperatures of 655  to 670 C. Demagnet-
ization responses of all samples were investigated by
principal component analysis [Kirschvink, 1980].
[10] TheTrujillohillstratigraphic sequenceexhibitsboth
normal and reversed polarity characteristic remanences.
Demagnetization responses varied and can be described as
four types. About one third (29%) of both normal and
reversed polarity samples (20 samples) displayed linear
demagnetization behavior above 300 –400 C, with lines
that trended to the origin of orthogonal axes vector plots
(Figures 2a and 2b). The MAD (maximum angular devia-
tion) values range from 0.5  to 4.5 ; these samples are
designated as ‘‘Group I.’’ Another 26% of the samples (18

Jurassic, Oxfordian-lower Kimmeridgian lower Morrison Formation (yellow); and late, Late Jurassic,
Kimmeridgian-Tithonian upper Morrison Formation (red). For reference, the averaged NA Late
Cretaceouspole(GlobermanandIrving,1998)isshowninmaroon.TheColoradoPlateauisshadedgray.

counterclockwiserotationaroundanEulerpolelocatedat34.6 N,254.6 E.ArrowsalongthepathAPW
pathindicatetheageprogressionofpaleopoles.(c)TheamountofrotationindicatedbyvariousColorado
Plateau paleopoles plotted againts paleopole age; clockwise (counterclockwise) rotation is positive
